answer.evidence: The stone foot (rows 37-45, width 10) has a light top band at rows 37-41 (L about 220, with a notch where the pole enters). Row 42 steps down to a darker front face (L about 197, then 176) with a dark bottom outline at row 45. That gives about 5 top rows and 4 front rows, so the foot reads as a 3/4 block, though the edge line is subtle. The pole is only 2 px wide and the banner is a flat hanging cloth drawn as a vertical face. The crossbar at rows 4-5 is a thin front-facing beam. The finial is decor. The foot is taken as the main body because it is the only solid volume.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin, sparse prop, so density is judged by eye. Measured facts are fine: 13 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage, 23% neutral dark edge pixels. Those numbers sit near the hedge (9) and below the stall (17) and well (20), and the outline is partly tinted, partly dark. At this scale the banner reads as a small icon. The blue cloth has about 3 tones, the gold border and star are mostly flat, and the pole and stone foot have only 2-3 steps with little grain, stone speckle or per-stone shading. The references (well, stall) have 5-6 steps with visible texture dots. The candidate looks a bit thinner and flatter than they do, closer to a clean sticker than to the Beodeul standard. Since the guidance is to fail when in doubt, this is a fail.
